scope: Proposition 4.8 of the manuscript “Baumslag-Solitar-free one-relator groups are hyperbolic” (preprints/Baumslag-Solitar-free-one-relator-groups-are-hyperbolic-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 258 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b578833682141115), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Every line L ∈ U determines an actual aligned bilateral path of positively traversed edges · · · , E−1, E0 = e, E1, · · · in T , with transferred lines in its successive edge frames. The following properties hold. (i) The path is independent of coset representatives and of compatible changes of frames and line coordinates. (ii) For every finite window containing E0, its stabilizer K ≤ P is finitely generated and noncyclic, and the endpoints of L lie in ΛK. (iii) Two distinct actual aligned windows of the same shape about e have at most cyclic common stabilizer. In particular, an irrational point can belong to the limit sets of at most one such window stabilizer. (iv) If an aligned one-sided window joins e to he, its stabilizer is S = P ∩ hPh−1. The boundary map of S −→ h−1 Sh, x 7−→ h−1 xh, implements its line transfer. On the irrational-endpoint domain it preserves µ; it takes its domain in U into U. In (iii), a shape specifies the numbers of edges before and after the central edge, all traversed positively.
